name: Creamy English Pea Salad with Bacon

cookwares.name: medium saucepan if using fresh peas

ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more for cooking water
freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste

instructions.primary_message: In a small bowl, add red onion, 1 tablespoon vinegar, and water and toss to combine; let sit at room temperature until ready to use, at least 15 minutes, or refrigerate up to 24 hours. When ready to use, drain and discard liquid.
In a large skillet, cook bacon over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until fat is rendered and bacon is crisp, 12 to 15 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer bacon to a paper towel–lined plate.

Meanwhile, if using fresh peas, bring a medium saucepan of salted water to a boil over high heat. Add fresh peas; cook until tender-crisp and bright green, about 1 minute. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool; drain well and pat dry with paper towels. If using frozen peas, ensure they are fully thawed, drained, and patted dry. (Frozen peas do not need to be blanched.)
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic, honey, salt, pepper, and remaining 1 tablespoon vinegar until smooth. Stir in chives, dill, and lemon zest.
Add peas, cheddar, and drained onions to bowl; fold gently until evenly coated. Stir in bacon just before serving.

schema_metadata.keywords: Pea salad, creamy pea salad with bacon

description: This creamy pea salad with bacon, cheddar, and herbs is an easy, make-ahead side for Easter, potlucks, and spring picnics.
notes:
Optional substitutions: shelled fresh sweet peas → thawed frozen peas

Notes: This recipe can easily be doubled.

Make-ahead and storage: The dressing can be made up to 2 days ahead and refrigerated in an airtight container until ready to use.
The salad can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days before serving. Keep cooked bacon separate and add just before serving for best texture.
author: Leah Colins
